text:
I can install the binary now. Setup needs your password and a Codeberg token, so you'll run that part yourself.

**1. Install the binary (I'll run this now; no root needed)**

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baney75/tentmaker/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --no-setup
tentmaker version --json
tentmaker status --json
```

Without root, the binary goes to `~/.local/bin`. If `tentmaker` isn't found afterward, use `~/.local/bin/tentmaker` or add that folder to your PATH. `status` should exit 4 ("not set up yet"), which is expected.

**2. Create the Codeberg token (you do this in a browser)**

On codeberg.org go to user settings > Applications, create a token with scopes `write:repository` and `read:user`, and copy it. I won't see it, and I won't put it in any command or file.

**3. Run setup in your own Terminal (you do this)**

```sh
sudo tentmaker setup --yes --forge forgejo --forge-url https://codeberg.org --repo me/notes --token-stdin
```

Paste the token, press Enter, then Ctrl-D. Setup asks for your sudo password here, which I can't enter. It sets up the sandbox and service, then runs `doctor`.

**4. Verify (I'll run this after you finish step 3)**

```sh
tentmaker doctor --json
tentmaker repo list --json
```

Codeberg runs in checks mode, so no workflow changes are needed. Tentmaker reads your workflow files, runs the jobs it supports, and posts commit statuses named `tentmaker/<job name>`.

**Before I go further, I need you to confirm:**

1. **Is `me/notes` the exact Codeberg owner and repo name?** If your username differs, tell me and I'll use that.
2. **Is the repo public or private?** If it's public, I'd add `--allow-public` after setup. That lets code from outside contributors run on this Mac once they're allowed to trigger CI, so I need your explicit yes before I add it. Private repos don't need it.
3. **Do you want these statuses to gate merges?** If so, you'd make `tentmaker/<job>` required in Codeberg branch protection. I can't change that for you, and I'd only suggest it.

Once you've confirmed those and finished step 3, I'll run the verification.
